scenario: A decoder-only model must answer from a 64k-token record, but GPU memory is exhausted at modest concurrency.
decision: Explain the dominant inference-memory pressure and compare remedies.
must_evidence: shorter retrieved context or cache-aware serving
trap: Attributing all inference memory to model weights.

scenario: Generation is repetitive and too deterministic after a configuration change.
decision: Diagnose decoding parameters without conflating them.
trap: Assuming temperature and top-p are interchangeable knobs.

scenario: A classifier must emit one of four labels, but sometimes adds explanations or invents labels.
decision: Design and evaluate constrained output behavior.
trap: Using prompt wording as the only enforcement layer.

scenario: A long system prompt improves the viewed examples but degrades an unseen slice.
decision: Determine whether the prompt change generalizes.
trap: Optimizing repeatedly on the reported test set.

scenario: Training and evaluation corpora contain near-duplicate support articles with different IDs.
trap: Deduplicating only by record ID.

scenario: A new tokenizer reduces English sequence length but expands code and multilingual samples.
must_evidence: model compatibility and embedding resize cost
trap: Choosing solely from aggregate English compression.

scenario: INT8 makes a checkpoint smaller but production latency does not improve.
trap: Equating checkpoint size reduction with latency improvement.

scenario: A team proposes pruning, distillation, and quantization as equivalent ways to compress a model.
decision: Choose and test an approach for the deployment constraint.
must_evidence: weights removed versus student training versus precision reduction
trap: Assuming identical artifacts and tradeoffs.

scenario: A small private dataset must adapt a large model on limited GPUs.
decision: Choose full tuning or PEFT and define validation.
trap: Claiming PEFT eliminates overfitting or privacy risk.

scenario: Preference data consists of chosen/rejected pairs, with no reliable reward model infrastructure.
decision: Compare DPO with RLHF and state when neither is justified.
must_evidence: direct pairwise objective versus reward-model/RL pipeline
trap: Selecting the newest preference method without validating labels.

scenario: ROUGE improves, but reviewers say summaries omit critical facts.
must_evidence: blinded human or calibrated judge protocol
trap: Treating reference overlap as semantic correctness.

scenario: An LLM judge strongly favors outputs from its own model family.
trap: Using judge scores as objective ground truth.

scenario: A model does not fit one GPU, and the cluster has fast links within nodes but slower links between nodes.
trap: Maximizing one form of parallelism without measuring communication.

scenario: Mixed precision training diverges intermittently after increasing effective batch size.
trap: Assuming every divergence is insufficient GPU memory.

scenario: Online traffic has variable prompt lengths and strict tail-latency objectives.
trap: Maximizing batch size using average latency alone.

scenario: A Triton-served candidate is healthy but silently uses a different tokenizer than training.
trap: Considering HTTP health sufficient deployment validation.

scenario: Latency and uptime are stable while citation faithfulness falls after a corpus update.
trap: Monitoring only infrastructure health.

scenario: A model rollout increases throughput but also refusal rate for one language.
decision: Make a ship or rollback decision.
trap: Averaging the harmed language into a global metric.

scenario: A medical assistant can reproduce rare training examples containing personal information.
trap: Relying on a warning banner as mitigation.

scenario: A toxicity guardrail reduces unsafe output but disproportionately blocks benign dialect content.
trap: Reporting only overall block accuracy.
